alright lets go further here. so first of all im not really a fan of this grey backing it all lands on, it should be transparent unless there is paint there. but also lets just do a side by side of our uv capability vs blockbench bar for bar. 

here is block bench adding a cylinder: [Image #1]

us adding a cylinder: [Image #2]

next

blockbench creating a texture map: [Image #3]

ours creating a texture map: [Image #4]

ok immediately we have some big disconnects here. first of all look at block bench again: [Image #5] ok its on a transparent background, and it has the cylinder top and bottom in the same shape. 

ours: [Image #6] no shape, random assortment, huge open grey space

theirs: [Image #7] the top piece here is one piece even though its segments

ours: [Image #8] segments, no single piece.

theirs: [Image #9][Image #10] can be further manipulated to how you wish [Image #11] break out a slice 

theirs: when rotating, there is a clear line where the rotation happens to be at level[Image #12] with a blue line

ours: [Image #13] no rotate control, no line to show when leveled on any axis
resolution: Replaced triangle-box UV editing with topology-aware connected islands: cylinder caps now pack as coherent radial pieces, exact face corners remain editable over a fixed atlas, detached faces rebuild seams atomically, unused atlas space is transparent, and island/face transforms plus rotation snapping are exposed in the full-height inspector.
